answer: Make influence accumulate like sediment, not appear on demand: every identity starts weightless and earns standing only by completing a rising ladder of public, verifiable tasks — first small checks, then harder reviews and bug hunts — recorded in a shared atlas of completed work. Each shale layer of proven effort takes real time, so progress moves at a glacier's pace and cannot be bought or cloned overnight; a farm would have to climb the whole ladder once per clone. The limit is access: first rungs must stay modest, or the ladder hardens into an incumbents' club.
